text.p: StockNet Inc said Tuesday it had temporarily removed its president, Paul R. Ruff, while its board completed an investigation of "apparent irregularities."
The action was taken at a recent emergency special meeting of the StockNet board, it said.
In a statement, the company alleged:

"Ruff had removed substantially all of the corporate funds from various depositories, had transferred some of the funds to a personal account, appeared to have become involved in a competitive business with a former consultant to StockNet, and had not appeared at the corporate offices for several days.
"To date, Ruff has refused to explain his actions."
It said its board had appointed Richard Rozzi as interim president, pending completion of an investigation of Ruff's actions.
It said its board has retained legal counsel which has taken immediate steps to recover the corporate funds and pursue any violation of corporate fiduciary duties and responsibilities.
A complete review of recent corporate actions and spending of corporate funds is under way, it added.
The company could not be immediately reached for comment.
StockNet was formed in February 1996 to develop financial, sports, entertainment and other specialized sites on the Internet to generate revenues from fees and advertising.
In October, the company announced the acquisition for $3.4 million in a stock swap of All Sports Inc, which maintains a site on the Internet that provides up-to-the-minute sports scores and stories.
In addition to AllSports, the company at the time said it had three other subsidiaries: FantasyStock, Informed Investor and Net Prophets.
